name: Biryani
description: Layered spiced rice with meat — the celebration pot.

ayurveda.note: Spice-heavy, meat-rich.

unani.note: Classic garam dish despite its thanda rice base.

histamine.note: Yogurt marinade + tomato + spices; reheated next-day biryani is notably worse.

name: Chicken karahi
description: Wok-fried chicken in a sharp tomato-ginger masala.

histamine.note: Tomato-dominant gravy — inherits tomato's score.

name: Dal tadka
description: Everyday lentils finished with a sizzling ghee tempering.

ayurveda.note: Mild — the everyday balanced dish.

histamine.note: Fresh-cooked dal is gentle; day-old less so.

name: Chana masala
description: Chickpeas in a dark spiced onion-tomato gravy.

histamine.note: Tomato gravy + amchur/anardana souring.

name: Aloo gobi
description: Dry-spiced potato and cauliflower.

ayurveda.note: Two cooling vegetables in warming spices — lands near neutral.

histamine.note: One of the safest desi dishes when reactive (skip the tomato variant).

name: Sarson ka saag
description: Slow-cooked mustard greens with makki roti — Punjab's winter ritual.

histamine.note: Palak-heavy versions inherit spinach's higher score.

name: Butter chicken
description: Tandoori chicken folded into a creamy tomato-butter gravy.

ayurveda.note: Sour-rich tomato-cream — heavy pitta load.

histamine.note: Tomato-concentrate gravy — inherits tomato's score.

name: Tandoori chicken
description: Yogurt-spice marinated chicken charred in the tandoor.

tcm.note: Dry-roasted over fire — TCM reads charring as heating.

histamine.note: Fresh off the grill is decent; the red color and long marination add little histamine.

name: Samosa
description: Deep-fried pastry triangle with spiced potato.

tcm.note: Deep-frying reads hot in every tradition.

histamine.note: Freshly fried is okay-ish; reused frying oil is an unquantified extra.

name: Pakora
description: Besan-battered fritters of rainy-day chai.

histamine.note: Spinach/eggplant pakoras inherit those vegetables' scores.

name: Haleem
description: Wheat, lentils, and meat pounded into a slow porridge.

unani.note: Prescribed as a strengthening garam food.

histamine.note: Hours of slow-cooking meat raises histamine — flavor and amines rise together.

name: Nihari
description: Overnight-simmered shank stew — the definitive winter garam dish.

unani.note: Old Delhi hakims' cold-weather prescription, literally.

histamine.note: Overnight meat simmering maximizes histamine — worst-case cooking method for the sensitive.

name: Khichdi
description: Soft rice and moong cooked together — the healing pot of the subcontinent.

tcm.note: Functionally TCM's congee logic.

ayurveda.note: THE sattvic recovery food — cooling, tridoshic.

histamine.note: Fresh khichdi is close to the ideal reactive-day meal.

name: Paratha
description: Ghee-layered griddled flatbread.

unani.note: Wheat + ghee + tawa = breakfast for cold mornings.

histamine.note: As wheat.

name: Sooji halwa
description: Semolina roasted in ghee, sweetened, and spooned warm.

unani.note: A prescribed warming sweet — halwa in winter, kheer in summer.

histamine.note: Benign components; cassia cinnamon garnish adds a touch.

name: Kheer
description: Slow-thickened rice-milk pudding.

ayurveda.note: Milk + rice + sugar: all three cooling — the summer sweet.

unani.note: Kheer/firni is the thanda counterpart to garam halwa.

histamine.note: Fresh is fine; nut garnishes add their own scores.

name: Hummus
description: Chickpea-tahini purée with lemon and garlic.

ayurveda.note: Tahini and garlic tilt it warm.

histamine.note: Fresh homemade is gentle; store tubs with citric acid/preservatives vary.

name: Falafel
description: Deep-fried herbed chickpea (or fava) fritters.

tcm.note: Deep-fried.

histamine.note: Egyptian ta'ameya uses fava — see the favism note on ful.

name: Shawarma
description: Marinated meat shaved off the vertical spit into bread.

histamine.note: Long-marinated meat rotating warm for hours — a histamine-friendly method it is not.

name: Kabsa / majboos
description: Gulf spiced rice with chicken and dried lime.

histamine.note: Tomato base + loomi (fermented dried lime).

name: Tabbouleh
description: Parsley salad flecked with bulgur, tomato, and lemon.

tcm.note: Raw herb salad.

histamine.note: Tomato + lemon carry the load; parsley and bulgur are innocent.

name: Fattoush
description: Chopped salad with sumac and fried bread shards.

unani.note: Sumac-dressed raw salad — cooling on balance.

histamine.note: Tomato again; skip it in the bowl and this drops to a 1.

name: Ful medames
description: Slow-stewed fava beans with cumin, lemon, and oil.

ayurveda.note: Bean is coolish; the cumin-garlic-oil dressing warms the dish.

unani.note: Cold-leaning bean deliberately corrected with garam dressing — classic Unani logic in a breakfast.

histamine.note: Long-held warm vats are worse than fresh pots; favism caution for G6PD.

name: Mujadara
description: Lentils and rice under a blanket of caramelized onions.

ayurveda.note: Near-balanced; fried onion tips it barely warm.

histamine.note: A gentle, reactive-friendly dish when fresh.

name: Kunafa
description: Crisp shredded pastry over molten cheese, drowned in syrup.

tcm.note: Rich-sweet-baked; not classical.

histamine.note: Fresh akkawi/mozzarella keeps it moderate — aged-cheese versions score worse.

name: Baklava
description: Nut-packed filo layers soaked in syrup.

ayurveda.note: Nuts + honey-syrup: everything in it is warming.

histamine.note: Walnut versions inherit the walnut liberator flag; pistachio versions are milder.

name: Fried rice
description: Day-old rice tossed hot with egg and soy.

tcm.note: Wok-frying warms neutral rice.

histamine.note: Built on leftover rice + soy sauce — two histamine strikes by design.

name: Chow mein
description: Stir-fried wheat noodles with vegetables.

histamine.note: Soy sauce carries the score.

name: Hot and sour soup
description: Peppery-vinegary soup with tofu and mushrooms.

tcm.note: White pepper + vinegar: deliberately warming and dispersing.

histamine.note: Vinegar + mushrooms + soy — a flare-day trap despite feeling medicinal.

name: Congee
description: Long-simmered rice porridge — China's khichdi.

tcm.note: THE recovery food; toppings shift its direction.

ayurveda.note: Reads like rice kanji.

histamine.note: Plain fresh congee is as safe as food gets.

name: Dumplings (jiaozi)
description: Wheat wrappers around pork-cabbage filling, boiled or fried.

tcm.note: Boiled neutral; fried guo tie warmer.

histamine.note: Fresh-made are fine; the dipping sauce (soy + vinegar) is the histamine event.

name: Mapo tofu
description: Silken tofu in a numbing-hot fermented bean sauce.

tcm.note: Chili + Sichuan pepper overwhelm cooling tofu.

histamine.note: Doubanjiang (fermented broad-bean chili paste) is a fermented histamine bomb.

name: Wonton soup
description: Delicate shrimp-pork parcels in clear broth.

histamine.note: Shrimp filling + long-held broth.

name: Hot pot
description: Communal simmering pot — typically mala-spiced.

tcm.note: The classic mala broth is deliberately heating; clear broths milder.

histamine.note: Broth simmers for hours while seafood cycles through it — score varies wildly with what you dip.

name: Stir-fried greens with garlic
description: Any leafy green flash-fried with garlic — the default vegetable plate.

tcm.note: Cooling greens, minimally warmed by garlic and the wok.

histamine.note: Safe if finished with salt; oyster sauce versions jump to 2-3.

name: Pizza
description: Flatbread with tomato sauce and melted cheese.

tcm.note: Not classical; baked-rich reads warm-damp.

ayurveda.note: Sour tomato + aged cheese + yeasted dough.

histamine.note: Tomato sauce + aged cheese + yeast — the weeknight histamine trifecta.

name: Burger
description: Grilled beef patty in a bun with fixings.

histamine.note: Ground beef ages fast + tomato + cheese slice; a plain fresh patty scores better.

name: French fries
description: Deep-fried potato batons.

tcm.note: Neutral potato turned hot by deep-frying.

histamine.note: Potato is innocent; old fryer oil and toppings are the wildcard.

name: Mac and cheese
description: Pasta folded into a cheddar sauce.

tcm.note: Rich-damp comfort food; not classical.

ayurveda.note: Aged cheese leads.

histamine.note: Aged cheddar is the whole point — and the whole problem.

name: Caesar salad
description: Romaine under parmesan, croutons, and anchovy dressing.

tcm.note: Raw salad base; rich dressing tempers it.

ayurveda.note: Leaf cool, dressing heating; net mild.

histamine.note: Parmesan + anchovies: two of the highest-histamine foods hiding in a 'light' salad.

name: Tomato soup
description: Smooth simmered tomato bowl.

tcm.note: Cool tomato served hot; reads near-neutral.

ayurveda.note: Concentrated sour tomato.

histamine.note: Tomato, concentrated — maximal form of the trigger.

name: Chicken noodle soup
description: The universal sickbed soup.

tcm.note: Chicken + broth + ginger logic: warming and restoring in every tradition.

histamine.note: The catch: long-simmered broth is high-histamine — quick-cooked versions are the reactive-safe route.

name: Spaghetti bolognese
description: Pasta under slow tomato-beef ragù.

histamine.note: Tomato concentrate + long-simmered ground beef + the parmesan on top.

name: Pancakes
description: Griddled sweet breakfast rounds.

tcm.note: Griddled wheat-egg-milk; not classical.

ayurveda.note: Components split; net mild.

histamine.note: Batter is benign; watch the toppings (chocolate, strawberries, aged butter).

name: Dosa
description: Fermented rice-and-dal batter spread thin and crisped on a griddle.

tcm.note: Read from rice and urad; the ferment adds a warming, sour quality.

ayurveda.note: Fermentation turns an otherwise shita batter — soured foods are ushna.

unani.note: Garam by its ferment, though the rice base is thanda.

histamine.note: Overnight batter fermentation — the crisp dosa is a fermented food, which surprises people.

name: Idli
description: Soft steamed discs of the same fermented batter — the gentlest breakfast there is.

tcm.note: Steamed and mild; the ferment is tempered by the cooking.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna, though laghu and easy to digest.

unani.note: Garam by ferment; still the lightest thing on the table.

histamine.note: Fermented batter, like dosa — light on the stomach but not low on histamine.

name: Sambar
description: Tamarind-soured toor dal with vegetables and its own spice blend.

tcm.note: Sour and heavily spiced over a neutral dal base.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa from tamarind plus ushna spices — heating despite the cooling dal.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; the tamarind and chilli dominate the thanda toor.

histamine.note: Tamarind-soured — the souring agent is what lifts it, not the dal.

name: Rasam
description: Thin peppery tamarind broth — drunk from the bowl, or poured over rice.

tcm.note: Black pepper and garlic in a thin broth — a warming, surface-releasing soup.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna; the household remedy given at the first sign of a cold.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, and taken exactly for that reason when someone is chilled.

histamine.note: Tamarind base; the pepper and chilli add irritation independent of histamine.

name: Upma
description: Roasted semolina cooked with mustard seed, curry leaf and onion.

tcm.note: Dry-roasted grain with warming tempering.

ayurveda.note: Roasting and the tempering spices push it ushna.

histamine.note: Low — unfermented, unlike its dosa and idli neighbours.

name: Uttapam
description: Thick dosa batter poured soft and studded with onion and tomato.

tcm.note: The rice base with vegetable toppings; read with dosa.

ayurveda.note: Fermented batter, so ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented batter plus tomato — both push it up.

name: Vada
description: Ring of ground urad batter, deep-fried to a crisp shell and soft middle.

tcm.note: Deep-fried and dense — warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Urad is ushna and guru to begin with; frying compounds it.

unani.note: Garam-tar; heavy, and famously hard to digest at night.

histamine.note: Urad batter is rested before frying, and the oil is usually well used.

name: Curd rice
description: Rice folded through yogurt with a mustard-seed tempering — the meal that ends a South Indian plate.

tcm.note: Rice and yogurt together, eaten cool — the classic settling dish.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna in the classical reading, however cooling the dish feels.

unani.note: Thanda-tar in desi usage; specifically given to cool a burning stomach.

histamine.note: Yogurt-based, and often eaten after sitting a while — both matter.

nutrition.highlight: how a South Indian plate ends

name: Rajma chawal
description: Kidney beans stewed thick in onion-tomato masala, ladled over rice.

tcm.note: Heavy beans in a spiced gravy.

ayurveda.note: Rajma is ushna and guru; the masala adds to it.

unani.note: Garam and windy — the reason hing and ginger go in.

histamine.note: Tomato-based gravy; tomato alone is already high.

name: Chole bhature
description: Spiced chickpeas with a huge deep-fried leavened bread.

tcm.note: Fried leavened bread plus a heavily spiced curry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna throughout — fermented dough, deep frying and hot masala together.

unani.note: Garam-khushk in a high degree; the classic heavy indulgence.

histamine.note: Fermented dough, tomato and amchur — several contributors at once.

name: Palak paneer
description: Pureed spinach with cubes of fresh cheese.

tcm.note: Spinach is cooling; paneer is neutral-cooling.

ayurveda.note: Both the greens and the fresh cheese are shita, though cream makes it guru.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the spices are what stop it being cold outright.

histamine.note: Spinach is a SIGHI 3 on its own — this dish is mostly spinach.

name: Matar paneer
description: Peas and fresh cheese in a tomato-onion gravy.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese and peas in a mildly spiced gravy.

ayurveda.note: Paneer and peas are both shita; the masala warms it somewhat.

histamine.note: Tomato gravy is the contributor here.

name: Baingan bharta
description: Eggplant charred whole over flame, peeled and mashed into masala.

tcm.note: Eggplant is cool in TCM; the charring adds warmth.

ayurveda.note: Vrintaka is ushna in the classical reading and traditionally avoided in excess.

unani.note: Baingan is garam in desi usage — one of the standard household 'heaty' vegetables.

histamine.note: Eggplant and tomato together — both sit high on the SIGHI list.

name: Bhindi masala
description: Sliced okra fried dry with onion and amchur so it never turns slimy.

tcm.note: Okra is cooling and moistening; dry-frying counters it.

ayurveda.note: Shita and slimy — the frying and amchur are there to cut that.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, which is why it is cooked dry and sour.

histamine.note: Low; amchur is the only real contributor.

nutrition.highlight: fried dry so it never slimes

name: Kadhi
description: Sour yogurt thickened with besan and simmered slowly with tempering.

tcm.note: Yogurt-based and eaten warm; cooling overall.

ayurveda.note: Soured dahi is firmly ushna — the classical reading, whatever the dish feels like.

unani.note: Thanda-tar in desi usage; the hing and methi tempering is there to make it digestible.

histamine.note: Deliberately soured yogurt, simmered long — high, and worth knowing on a reactive day.

name: Korma
description: Meat braised gently in yogurt, ground nuts and whole spice — rich, not fiery.

tcm.note: Meat and nuts with warm aromatics, cooked slowly.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — meat, nuts, yogurt and ghee together.

unani.note: Garam-tar; a strengthening dish of the Mughal table.

histamine.note: Yogurt marinade and slow cooking; nuts add a little more.

name: Rogan josh
description: Kashmiri lamb curry, deep red from chilli rather than tomato.

tcm.note: Lamb with heavy chilli and warm spice — hot throughout.

ayurveda.note: Mamsa plus ushna spices; among the most heating dishes in the set.

unani.note: Garam-khushk in a high degree — winter food in the valley.

histamine.note: Yogurt-braised lamb; the chilli adds irritation on its own account.

name: Keema
description: Minced meat browned hard and simmered with peas and masala.

tcm.note: Minced red meat with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; mamsa with a full masala.

histamine.note: Mince has far more cut surface than a whole cut, so it climbs faster — cook it the day you buy it.

name: Seekh kebab
description: Spiced mince pressed onto skewers and cooked over coals.

tcm.note: Mince over direct fire with hot spice — hot by both meat and method.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree; grilling is the most heating way to cook.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; classic winter and celebration food.

histamine.note: Minced meat, often rested with papaya as a tenderiser — which adds a liberator.

nutrition.highlight: pressed onto skewers, cooked on coals

name: Pav bhaji
description: Mashed vegetables cooked down with butter and spice, with soft rolls to mop it.

tcm.note: Heavily buttered and spiced vegetable mash.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the masala and butter, over a cooling vegetable base.

histamine.note: Tomato-heavy and cooked down, on a leavened bread — several high contributors together.

name: Gulab jamun
description: Fried khoya dumplings soaked through with cardamom syrup.

tcm.note: Fried and sweet — warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru; fried khoya in sugar syrup.

unani.note: Garam-tar, the archetype of the heavy desi sweet.

histamine.note: Low; the khoya and sugar are both modest on this scale.

name: Jalebi
description: Fermented batter piped in spirals, fried, and dunked in saffron syrup.

tcm.note: Fermented, fried and sugared — hot on every count.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree; the ferment and the frying compound each other.

unani.note: Garam-tar; eaten hot with milk on winter mornings.

histamine.note: The batter is deliberately fermented overnight before frying.

name: Rasgulla
description: Chenna balls boiled in light sugar syrup until they swell and turn spongy.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese in a light syrup — the least heavy of the sweets.

ayurveda.note: Chenna is shita and unfried; unusual among mithai for staying cooling.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, unlike the fried and khoya sweets.

histamine.note: Low; fresh cheese and sugar syrup.

name: Barfi
description: Khoya cooked down with sugar and set into diamonds.

tcm.note: Reduced milk and sugar — warming and heavy.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru, though khoya's classical reading is contested.

histamine.note: Low; nuts and khoya are both modest.

name: Kulfi
description: Milk boiled down for hours, then frozen dense on a stick — no churning.

tcm.note: Frozen dairy is cold, whatever it was before freezing.

ayurveda.note: Shita and very guru — a heavy cold sweet.

histamine.note: Low; the long reduction is a flavour choice, not a histamine one.

name: Baba ganoush
description: Charred eggplant whipped with tahini, lemon and garlic.

tcm.note: Eggplant is cool; the tahini and garlic warm it.

ayurveda.note: Vrintaka is ushna, and the tahini adds to it.

unani.note: Baingan is garam in the eastern reading; the lemon does not cool it much.

histamine.note: Eggplant plus lemon — eggplant alone sits high on the SIGHI list.

name: Muhammara
description: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip, sharpened with pomegranate.

tcm.note: Roasted peppers and walnuts — warming throughout.

ayurveda.note: Walnut and chilli are both ushna.

histamine.note: Walnuts are a liberator, the peppers are dried, and the pomegranate molasses is concentrated.

name: Maqluba
description: Rice, fried vegetables and meat layered in a pot and turned out upside down.

tcm.note: Fried vegetables and meat over rice, spiced with baharat.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the meat and warm spice; the rice is shita underneath.

histamine.note: Fried eggplant and a long cook are the contributors.

name: Koshari
description: Egypt's street plate — rice, lentils and pasta under fried onion and tomato sauce.

tcm.note: Grains and lentils; the sauce and fried onion warm it.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the sauce and frying, over a cooling grain base.

histamine.note: Vinegared tomato sauce over the top — that is what lifts an otherwise plain plate.

name: Molokhia
description: Finely chopped jute leaves cooked to a green, deliberately viscous stew.

tcm.note: A leafy green stew; the garlic tempering warms it.

ayurveda.note: Leafy and mucilaginous — shita, like the other slippery greens.

unani.note: Thanda-tar in the Egyptian and Levantine reading, though served hot.

histamine.note: Leafy green base with a long cook; the garlic-coriander tempering adds little.

name: Kibbeh
description: Bulgur and minced meat shells stuffed with more spiced meat and pine nuts, then fried.

tcm.note: Fried minced meat with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — mamsa, frying and baharat together.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; the centrepiece of a Levantine table.

histamine.note: Minced meat, and often prepared hours ahead — both matter.

nutrition.highlight: shell of bulgur, heart of meat

name: Manakish
description: Flatbread baked with a thick paste of zaatar and olive oil.

tcm.note: Leavened bread with warming herbs.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: leavened dough plus thyme and sumac.

histamine.note: Yeasted dough; the sumac in zaatar is sour and adds a little.

name: Harira
description: Moroccan lentil and chickpea soup, thickened and soured — the Ramadan bowl.

tcm.note: A long-simmered pulse soup with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the spicing; the pulses themselves are shita.

unani.note: Garam-tar; taken to break the fast for exactly that reason.

histamine.note: Tomato-based and simmered long, then often kept warm for hours before serving.

name: Tagine
description: Meat and fruit cooked slowly in a conical clay pot until it falls apart.

tcm.note: Slow-cooked meat with dried fruit and warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: mamsa, dried fruit and baharat all point the same way.

histamine.note: Long slow cooking plus dried fruit — both are histamine contributors, and this dish is defined by them.

nutrition.highlight: meat and fruit, cooked to collapse

name: Warak enab
description: Vine leaves rolled tight around rice, herbs and lemon, then steamed.

tcm.note: Rice and herbs with lemon, eaten cool or at room temperature.

ayurveda.note: Shita from the rice and leaves; the lemon is sour but the dish reads cooling.

unani.note: Thanda; a summer mezze, often served cold.

histamine.note: Brined vine leaves and lemon — the leaves are preserved, which is the contributor.

name: Kung pao chicken
description: Diced chicken with peanuts and dried chillies in a sweet-sour-numbing sauce.

tcm.note: Dried chilli and Sichuan pepper over chicken — hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Soy sauce and rice vinegar are both fermented; peanuts and chilli are both liberators.

nutrition.highlight: sweet, sour and numbing at once

name: Sweet and sour pork
description: Battered pork tossed in a bright sauce of vinegar, sugar and pineapple.

tcm.note: Deep-fried and sauced; pork itself is neutral-cool.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the frying and the sour sauce.

histamine.note: Vinegar, ketchup and pineapple together — three contributors in one sauce.

name: Peking duck
description: Duck air-dried and roasted for crisp skin, eaten in pancakes with hoisin.

tcm.note: Roast duck is warming; duck itself is cooler than chicken.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — roasted fatty meat.

histamine.note: The duck is deliberately air-dried for a day or more before roasting, and hoisin is fermented.

name: Spring rolls
description: Shredded vegetables rolled in thin wrappers and deep-fried crisp.

tcm.note: Deep-fried; the filling is cooling, the method is not.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the frying, over shita vegetables.

histamine.note: Soy sauce in the filling is the main contributor; frying oil age is a separate issue.

name: Egg drop soup
description: Beaten egg swirled into simmering broth so it sets in ribbons.

tcm.note: A light broth with egg — gentle and neutral.

ayurveda.note: Egg is ushna in the classical reading, however light the soup.

unani.note: Garam-tar; a warming, easily digested soup.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator and the broth is long-simmered — a light soup with a heavy histamine load.

name: Lasagna
description: Sheets of pasta layered with meat sauce, béchamel and cheese, baked.

tcm.note: Baked meat and cheese — warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru: meat, cheese and refined wheat together.

histamine.note: Aged cheese plus long-cooked tomato sauce — and it is usually better the next day, which makes it worse here.

name: Risotto
description: Rice stirred with stock a ladle at a time until it turns creamy.

tcm.note: Rice with stock and cheese; mild and neutral.

ayurveda.note: Rice is shita, though the cheese and butter make it guru.

unani.note: Rice base, warmed by the stock and cheese.

histamine.note: Long-simmered stock, aged cheese and usually white wine — three high contributors in one pan.

name: Scrambled eggs
description: Eggs beaten and stirred over low heat until they just set.

tcm.note: Egg is neutral; butter adds a little warmth.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna in the classical reading — a heating breakfast.

unani.note: Garam-tar; eggs are firmly garam in desi and Unani usage.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator on the SIGHI list — the white more than the yolk.

name: Fish and chips
description: White fish in beer batter, deep-fried, with thick-cut chips.

tcm.note: Deep-fried; the fish itself is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — frying plus matsya, which is already heating.

histamine.note: Depends almost entirely on how fresh the fish was; the batter is usually beer-based.

name: Greek salad
description: Cucumber, tomato, onion and olives under a slab of feta and olive oil.

tcm.note: Raw vegetables, eaten cold — cooling throughout.

ayurveda.note: Shita from the raw vegetables; the cheese and olives temper it.

histamine.note: Tomato, olives and feta together — three of the higher-rated items in one bowl, which is why a 'light salad' can still flare someone.

name: Appam
description: Lacy-edged rice pancake with a soft thick middle, fermented with coconut.

tcm.note: Rice base; the ferment warms it.

ayurveda.note: Fermented batter is ushna.

unani.note: Garam by ferment, over a thanda rice base.

histamine.note: Overnight fermented batter, like dosa.

name: Idiyappam
description: Rice-flour noodles pressed into nests and steamed — eaten with coconut milk or curry.

tcm.note: Steamed rice flour; mild and neutral.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu — unfermented, so lighter than appam.

histamine.note: Very low — steamed rice flour and nothing else.

name: Puttu
description: Ground rice layered with grated coconut and steamed in a bamboo tube.

tcm.note: Steamed rice and coconut.

ayurveda.note: Shita from both rice and coconut.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Pesarattu
description: Andhra dosa ground from whole green gram — no rice, no fermentation.

tcm.note: Moong is cold; the ginger and chilli temper it.

ayurveda.note: Mudga is shita and the lightest pulse — and this batter is not fermented.

histamine.note: Low — unfermented, which sets it apart from every other dosa.

name: Avial
description: Every vegetable in the house in a loose coconut-and-yogurt gravy, finished with raw coconut oil.

tcm.note: Coconut and mixed vegetables, lightly soured.

ayurveda.note: Shita from coconut and the vegetables; the dahi is ushna classically.

histamine.note: Yogurt-soured and made in quantity to sit through a meal.

name: Thoran
description: Finely chopped vegetables tossed dry with grated coconut and mustard seed.

tcm.note: Vegetables and coconut, cooked briefly.

ayurveda.note: Shita; light and dry.

histamine.note: Very low — fresh vegetables, cooked and eaten the same day.

name: Lemon rice
description: Cooked rice tossed with turmeric, peanuts, curry leaf and a great deal of lemon.

tcm.note: Rice with citrus; the tempering warms it.

ayurveda.note: Nimbu is amla-rasa and ushna, over a shita rice base.

unani.note: Thanda in practice — a lunchbox rice for hot days.

histamine.note: Lemon-based, and peanuts add a second liberator.

name: Tamarind rice
description: Rice folded through a dark tamarind and sesame paste — temple food that keeps for a day.

tcm.note: Sour, spiced and sesame-rich.

ayurveda.note: Amlika is ushna; with sesame oil and chilli it is firmly heating.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, though tamarind alone is thanda in Unani.

histamine.note: Tamarind-heavy and made to sit — the keeping is the point and also the problem.

name: Coconut rice
description: Rice tossed with fried coconut, dal and cashew.

tcm.note: Rice and coconut with a light tempering.

ayurveda.note: Shita from both rice and coconut.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Bisi bele bath
description: Karnataka one-pot of rice, toor dal, vegetables and a dark roasted spice blend.

tcm.note: Spice-heavy and tamarind-soured.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: roasted masala, tamarind and ghee together.

histamine.note: Tamarind-soured and slow-cooked.

nutrition.highlight: a whole meal in one pot

name: Adai
description: Thick coarse dosa ground from four dals with chilli — protein-dense and unfermented.

tcm.note: Mixed dals with chilli, cooked thick.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: urad and chana with red chilli.

histamine.note: Low — the batter is used fresh, not fermented.

name: Payasam
description: Milk or coconut milk simmered with vermicelli or rice and jaggery.

tcm.note: Sweet milk, slowly reduced.

ayurveda.note: Milk is shita; the jaggery and cardamom warm it.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, though gur-based versions read garam.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Mysore pak
description: Besan cooked in an alarming quantity of ghee with sugar until it sets porous.

tcm.note: Ghee-heavy and cooked hot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — besan is shita but the ghee and sugar dominate.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Kuzhambu
description: Thick dark tamarind gravy with sesame oil and no dal — poured over rice.

tcm.note: Sour and sesame-rich.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: tamarind, sesame oil and chilli.

histamine.note: Heavily tamarind-based.

name: Dal makhani
description: Whole urad and rajma simmered overnight with butter and cream.

tcm.note: Slow-cooked pulses enriched with dairy.

ayurveda.note: Urad is ushna and guru; overnight cooking with butter compounds it.

unani.note: Garam-tar; among the heaviest dals there is.

histamine.note: Cooked overnight and reheated — the long hold is what rates it, not the dal.

name: Shahi paneer
description: Paneer in a pale cashew-and-cream gravy, mild and rich rather than hot.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese with nuts and cream.

ayurveda.note: Cashews and cream are guru and ushna; paneer is shita beneath.

histamine.note: Cream and cashew base; tomato in some versions raises it.

name: Malai kofta
description: Fried paneer-and-potato dumplings in a sweet creamy gravy.

tcm.note: Fried, then sauced richly.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — frying plus cream plus nuts.

histamine.note: Fried and cream-based; the koftas are usually made ahead.

name: Dum aloo
description: Baby potatoes pricked, fried and simmered in a deep red yogurt gravy.

tcm.note: Fried potato in a spiced yogurt gravy.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: frying, chilli and fennel over a shita potato.

histamine.note: Yogurt-braised and chilli-heavy.

name: Jeera aloo
description: Boiled potatoes tossed dry with cumin, turmeric and green chilli.

tcm.note: Cumin-forward and dry-cooked.

ayurveda.note: Jiraka is ushna; potato is shita beneath it.

histamine.note: Very low — no tomato, no dairy, no ferment.

name: Aloo paratha
description: Wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and shallow-fried in ghee.

tcm.note: Fried flatbread with a starchy filling.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — ghee-fried wheat.

histamine.note: Low; served with dahi and achar, which are not.

name: Poori
description: Small wholewheat rounds deep-fried until they balloon.

tcm.note: Deep-fried; hot and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru in a high degree.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; heavy, and famously hard to digest.

histamine.note: Low in itself; the oil's age matters more than the bread.

name: Kachori
description: Flaky fried pastry with a dry spiced dal or onion filling.

tcm.note: Deep-fried with a heating filling.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — fried maida with hing and chilli.

histamine.note: Fried and often sold hours old; the filling is made in advance.

name: Dahi vada
description: Fried urad dumplings soaked soft and drowned in sweetened yogurt with chutneys.

tcm.note: Fried, then soaked and served cold in yogurt.

ayurveda.note: Urad and frying are ushna; the dahi is classically ushna too, though the dish is served to cool.

unani.note: Thanda-tar in desi usage — a summer chaat.

histamine.note: Yogurt, tamarind chutney and soaking time together — high, despite feeling light.

name: Pani puri
description: Hollow crisp shells filled with spiced water, tamarind and potato — eaten one at a time, whole.

tcm.note: The mint-and-cumin water is cooling; the shell is fried.

ayurveda.note: Amchur, tamarind and chilli are all ushna.

unani.note: The pani is thanda; the puri is garam — the dish is both at once.

histamine.note: Tamarind and amchur water, standing in a pot — the sourness and the standing both count.

name: Bhel puri
description: Puffed rice tossed at the last second with onion, chutneys and sev.

tcm.note: Puffed rice with raw onion and sour chutneys.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the chutneys and onion.

histamine.note: Tamarind chutney is the contributor — the puffed rice itself is nothing.

name: Vada pav
description: A fried potato dumpling in a soft bun with dry garlic chutney.

tcm.note: Fried, in leavened bread, with chilli and garlic.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fried with a yeasted bun; the chutney is garlic and chilli.

name: Misal pav
description: Sprouted moth beans under a fiery red oil-slicked gravy, with farsan and bread.

tcm.note: Chilli-heavy and oil-topped.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — matki is warming and the kat is chilli and oil.

histamine.note: Chilli-heavy with a yeasted bun; the sprouts themselves are fine.

nutrition.highlight: the red oil on top is the point

name: Dhokla
description: Fermented besan batter steamed into a soft yellow sponge and tempered with mustard seed.

tcm.note: Steamed and light; besan is cooling beneath the ferment.

ayurveda.note: The ferment turns an otherwise shita batter.

unani.note: Thanda in desi usage — a light Gujarati breakfast.

histamine.note: Fermented batter, though steamed rather than fried.

name: Khandvi
description: Besan and buttermilk cooked to a paste, spread paper-thin and rolled.

tcm.note: Buttermilk-based and served cool.

ayurveda.note: Takra is ushna classically; besan is shita.

histamine.note: Buttermilk base.

name: Thepla
description: Wholewheat flatbread kneaded with fenugreek leaves — made to survive a long journey.

tcm.note: Wheat with methi and oil.

ayurveda.note: Methi is ushna and deepana.

histamine.note: Low — the reason it travels well is that it keeps without spoiling.

name: Litti chokha
description: Wheat balls stuffed with spiced sattu, roasted on coals, served with mashed vegetables.

tcm.note: Roasted on open fire with a roasted-gram filling.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the roasting; sattu itself is cooling.

histamine.note: The chokha is charred tomato and eggplant — both high.

name: Makki di roti
description: Coarse cornmeal flatbread patted by hand — it cracks, and that is normal.

tcm.note: Read with corn, which is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and ruksha; a winter bread.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; eaten with saag and gur through the cold months.

histamine.note: Very low — no yeast, no ferment, one ingredient.

name: Pulao
description: Rice cooked in stock with whole spice — lighter and simpler than biryani.

tcm.note: Rice cooked in meat stock with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the stock and spices, over shita rice.

histamine.note: Stock-based; a long-simmered yakhni raises it.

name: Jeera rice
description: Rice tempered with cumin in ghee — the default accompaniment to any dal.

tcm.note: Rice with a cumin tempering.

ayurveda.note: Jiraka is ushna; rice is shita.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Egg curry
description: Boiled eggs halved into an onion-tomato gravy.

tcm.note: Egg is neutral; the gravy is warming.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna and the masala adds to it.

unani.note: Garam-tar; eggs are firmly garam in desi usage.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator and the tomato gravy is high — together they add up.

name: Fish curry
description: Fish simmered briefly in a sour, spiced gravy — tamarind in the south, mustard in the east.

tcm.note: Fish with sour and pungent spicing.

ayurveda.note: Matsya is ushna and the souring agents add to it.

unani.note: Garam-tar; and famously never eaten with milk.

histamine.note: Depends heavily on the fish's freshness; the tamarind adds a liberator.

name: Prawn curry
description: Prawns cooked fast in coconut or tomato gravy — a minute too long and they turn to rubber.

tcm.note: Shellfish with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — prawns are the heating end of the seafood group.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator plus a tomato or tamarind base.

nutrition.highlight: a minute too long and it's rubber

name: Gajar halwa
description: Grated carrot cooked down in milk with ghee and khoya until it darkens.

tcm.note: Long reduction in milk with ghee.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — the winter sweet, eaten hot.

unani.note: Garam-tar; a cold-weather dish by design.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Besan ladoo
description: Besan roasted slowly in ghee until it smells nutty, then bound with sugar.

tcm.note: Roasted flour in ghee.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru, though besan alone is shita — the ghee and roasting decide it.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Motichoor ladoo
description: Tiny fried besan pearls soaked in syrup and pressed into balls.

tcm.note: Fried and syrup-soaked.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Kaju katli
description: Ground cashew and sugar rolled thin and cut into diamonds, sometimes silver-leafed.

tcm.note: Nut-based and sweet.

ayurveda.note: Kaju is ushna and snigdha.

histamine.note: Low.

nutrition.highlight: thin enough to see through, nearly

name: Rabri
description: Milk reduced for hours, the skin folded back in repeatedly until it is thick with layers.

tcm.note: Hours of reduction.

ayurveda.note: Milk keeps its shita virya classically, however far reduced — the same argument as khoya.

unani.note: Garam-tar in desi usage — a rich winter sweet.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Phirni
description: Ground rice set in sweetened milk and chilled in earthenware bowls.

tcm.note: Set and served cold.

ayurveda.note: Rice and milk are both shita; served chilled.

unani.note: Thanda-tar — an Eid sweet, and a summer one.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Sheer khurma
description: Vermicelli simmered in milk with dates and nuts — the Eid morning bowl.

tcm.note: Milk with dates and nuts, warm-spiced.

ayurveda.note: Dates and nuts are ushna over a shita milk base.

histamine.note: Dates and dried fruit are the contributors.

name: Halwa puri
description: Sunday breakfast: sooji halwa, fried puri and a chana curry, all on one plate.

tcm.note: Everything on the plate is fried or sweet.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree throughout.

histamine.note: Fried, and the chana is tomato-based.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached directly in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, eaten from the pan.

tcm.note: Tomato and pepper cooked down, with egg.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna and the sauce is chilli-spiced.

histamine.note: Tomato reduced down plus egg — one of the highest breakfasts there is, for something that looks so plain.

name: Mansaf
description: Lamb cooked in fermented dried-yogurt sauce over rice — Jordan's national dish, eaten by hand.

tcm.note: Lamb with a fermented dairy sauce.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: mamsa with soured dairy and warm spice.

histamine.note: Jameed is dried fermented yogurt — a long ferment, on lamb, held hot.

name: Mandi
description: Meat and rice cooked in a pit oven so the smoke and dripping fat flavour the grain.

tcm.note: Slow pit-roasted meat over rice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; roasting is the most heating method.

histamine.note: Slow-cooked meat, usually held warm before serving.

name: Fatteh
description: Layers of toasted bread, chickpeas and garlicky yogurt, topped with fried nuts.

tcm.note: Yogurt-based and served warm rather than hot.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna; the garlic and fried nuts add to it.

histamine.note: Yogurt and toasted bread, assembled ahead.

name: Sambousek
description: Half-moon pastries filled with cheese, spinach or spiced meat, then fried or baked.

tcm.note: Fried pastry with a savoury filling.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Fried, and the cheese versions carry more.

name: Batata harra
description: Fried potato cubes tossed with coriander, garlic and chilli.

tcm.note: Fried with garlic and chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Low — no dairy, no tomato, no ferment.

name: Shish tawook
description: Chicken marinated in yogurt, garlic and lemon, then grilled on skewers.

tcm.note: Grilled poultry with a sour marinade.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: chicken, garlic and grilling together.

histamine.note: Yogurt-and-lemon marinade, usually overnight — the marinating time is what counts.

name: Basbousa
description: Semolina cake soaked in syrup while still hot, cut into diamonds.

tcm.note: Baked and syrup-soaked.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Maamoul
description: Shortbread pressed in carved moulds around date or nut paste — Eid and Easter both.

tcm.note: Butter pastry with a date filling.

ayurveda.note: Dates and ghee are ushna.

histamine.note: Date-filled, and dried fruit is the contributor.

name: Umm Ali
description: Pastry torn into hot milk with nuts and raisins, then baked until the top blisters.

tcm.note: Baked milk pudding with nuts.

ayurveda.note: Nuts and raisins are ushna over a milk base.

histamine.note: Raisins and nuts, in milk, baked and often reheated.

name: Shorbat adas
description: Red lentils cooked to a smooth purée with cumin and lemon — the first thing at iftar.

tcm.note: A warm pulse soup with cumin.

ayurveda.note: Masoor is ushna in the classical reading; cumin adds to it.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; taken to open the fast for that reason.

histamine.note: Lemon at the end is the only real contributor.

name: Dan dan noodles
description: Noodles under chilli oil, sesame paste and minced pork — mixed at the table.

tcm.note: Chilli oil and Sichuan pepper — hot and numbing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Preserved vegetable, soy and chilli oil together.

name: Beef noodle soup
description: Noodles in a long-simmered spiced beef broth with braised shin.

tcm.note: Long-simmered beef broth with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: mamsa broth with five-spice.

histamine.note: Hours of broth on beef bones, plus soy — the same trap as bone broth.

name: Char siu
description: Pork marinated in hoisin and honey, then roasted until the edges char red.

tcm.note: Roasted and sweet-glazed.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Hoisin and soy marinade, and the pork is marinated overnight.

name: Baozi
description: Soft leavened buns steamed around a savoury or sweet filling.

tcm.note: Leavened dough, steamed.

ayurveda.note: Fermented dough is ushna.

histamine.note: Yeasted dough; the char siu filling raises it further.

name: Siu mai
description: Open-topped pork and prawn dumplings in a thin wrapper — the dim sum default.

tcm.note: Steamed pork and prawn.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: prawns and pork together.

histamine.note: Prawn is a liberator and the filling includes soy and dried mushroom.

name: Har gow
description: Translucent tapioca-starch wrappers pleated around whole prawns.

tcm.note: Steamed prawn in a starch wrapper.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; prawns are the heating end of seafood.

histamine.note: Prawn liberator, and the filling is made ahead.

nutrition.highlight: you should see the prawn through it

name: Xiao long bao
description: Dumplings holding a mouthful of hot soup, set as jelly in the filling before steaming.

tcm.note: Pork and aspic, steamed.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — the aspic is reduced broth.

histamine.note: The soup inside is set from long-simmered stock — that is the whole technique, and the whole problem.

nutrition.highlight: the soup is set as jelly

name: Scallion pancake
description: Laminated unleavened dough coiled with spring onion and fried flat.

tcm.note: Fried dough with allium.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from frying and the spring onion.

histamine.note: Low — unleavened, and made fresh.

name: Twice-cooked pork
description: Pork belly boiled, sliced, then stir-fried hard with bean paste and leeks.

tcm.note: Fried after boiling, with fermented bean paste.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Doubanjiang is a long-fermented broad bean and chilli paste — high, and central to the dish.

name: General Tso's chicken
description: Battered fried chicken in a sweet, sour and mildly hot glaze — American-Chinese, not Chinese.

tcm.note: Fried and chilli-glazed.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Soy, vinegar and chilli in the glaze, on deep-fried chicken.

name: Century egg congee
description: Rice porridge with century egg and shredded pork, cooked until the grains dissolve.

tcm.note: Rice porridge; the egg is cooling, the pork neutral.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the egg and pork over shita rice.

histamine.note: Century egg is months-cured and the congee simmers long — a gentle-seeming bowl that is not.

name: Salt and pepper squid
description: Squid in a light starch coating, fried hard and tossed with chilli, salt and pepper.

tcm.note: Fried seafood with pepper and chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; seafood fried hot.

histamine.note: Squid is a liberator and spoils fast; frying does not change that.

name: Omelette
description: Beaten eggs cooked flat and folded — plain, or around whatever is in the fridge.

tcm.note: Egg is neutral; butter warms it.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna — a heating breakfast in the classical reading.

unani.note: Garam-tar; eggs are firmly garam in desi and Unani usage.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator; cheese or tomato fillings raise it further.

name: French toast
description: Bread soaked in egg and milk, fried in butter, dusted with sugar.

tcm.note: Fried bread with egg and dairy.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru — egg, bread and butter together.

histamine.note: Egg liberator on yeasted bread, fried — several contributors at once.

name: Granola
description: Oats baked with honey, oil and nuts until clustered and crisp.

tcm.note: Baked oats with honey and nuts.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: oats, honey and nuts are all warming.

histamine.note: Dried fruit and nuts are the contributors, not the oats.

name: Sandwich
description: Whatever is to hand, between two slices of bread.

tcm.note: Depends entirely on the filling; the bread is the only constant.

ayurveda.note: Leavened bread is ushna; the filling decides the rest.

histamine.note: The bread is yeasted and the fillings are usually cured meat or cheese — which is where the rating really comes from.

name: Fried chicken
description: Chicken in seasoned flour, deep-fried until the crust shatters.

tcm.note: Deep-fried poultry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree — chicken is ushna and frying compounds it.

histamine.note: Often brined in buttermilk overnight, which is what lifts it above plain chicken.

name: Roast chicken
description: A whole bird roasted with fat and herbs until the skin crisps.

tcm.note: Roasted poultry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; roasting is a heating method.

histamine.note: Low when fresh and eaten hot. The leftovers are the problem — cooked chicken climbs fast in the fridge.

name: Beef stew
description: Beef and root vegetables cooked low for hours until the meat gives way.

tcm.note: Long slow braise.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Hours of simmering on meat, usually with tomato and wine — and better the next day, which makes it worse here.

name: Chili con carne
description: Minced beef and beans stewed long with chilli and cumin.

tcm.note: Chilli-heavy meat stew.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Tomato, chilli, beans and a long cook — high on several counts at once.

name: Paella
description: Saffron rice cooked flat and undisturbed until a toasted crust forms underneath.

tcm.note: Saffron rice with seafood or meat.

ayurveda.note: Saffron is ushna; the rice is shita beneath.

histamine.note: Shellfish and stock — the seafood versions especially.

nutrition.highlight: the crust underneath is the point

name: Carbonara
description: Pasta bound with egg, hard cheese and cured pork — no cream, ever.

tcm.note: Egg and cured pork over wheat pasta.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru.

histamine.note: Cured pork and aged cheese with raw egg — three high items and no cooking to soften them.

name: Cheesecake
description: Cream cheese set over a crushed-biscuit base, baked or chilled.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese and cream, served cold.

ayurveda.note: Shita and extremely guru.

histamine.note: Cream cheese is fresh and low; the base and toppings decide the rest.

name: Chicken 65
description: Fried chicken bites in a red chilli-curry-leaf coat — Madras, not Chinese.

tcm.note: Fried and chilli-heavy.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Yogurt-marinated and chilli-coated.

name: Chilli chicken
description: Battered chicken tossed with capsicum, soy and green chilli — India's own Chinese food.

tcm.note: Fried with soy and chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Soy sauce and vinegar over fried chicken.

name: Gobi manchurian
description: Battered cauliflower in a sweet-hot soy glaze — dry or gravy, never in between.

tcm.note: Fried and soy-glazed.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; the cauliflower beneath is shita.

histamine.note: Soy and vinegar glaze on deep-fried florets.

name: Chilli paneer
description: Paneer cubes fried and tossed in the same soy-chilli glaze.

tcm.note: Fried cheese in a soy glaze.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; paneer is shita underneath.

histamine.note: Soy and vinegar based.

name: Hakka noodles
description: Wheat noodles stir-fried hard with shredded vegetables and soy.

tcm.note: Stir-fried noodles with soy.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the frying and soy.

histamine.note: Soy sauce carries it.

name: Schezwan fried rice
description: Fried rice with a fiery red sauce that has little to do with Sichuan.

tcm.note: Chilli-paste fried rice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Fermented chilli paste and soy together.

name: Manchow soup
description: Dark peppery soup under a pile of fried noodles.

tcm.note: Peppery and soy-based.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Soy and stock base.

nutrition.highlight: the fried noodles on top are the point

name: Sweetcorn soup
description: Thick pale soup of creamed corn and cornflour, mild and faintly sweet.

tcm.note: Corn is neutral; the stock warms it.

ayurveda.note: Shita, following corn.

histamine.note: Stock-based; otherwise gentle.

nutrition.highlight: the mild one on every menu

name: Honey chilli potato
description: Twice-fried potato batons in a sticky sweet-hot glaze with sesame.

tcm.note: Fried and chilli-glazed.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Soy, vinegar and chilli sauce.

name: Momos
description: Himalayan steamed dumplings served with a fiery tomato-sesame chutney.

tcm.note: Steamed dough with a meat or vegetable filling.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the filling and chutney.

histamine.note: The chutney is tomato- and chilli-based, which rates higher than the dumpling.

name: Thukpa
description: Himalayan noodle soup with vegetables or meat in a light broth.

tcm.note: A warm broth noodle soup.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the broth and spice.

histamine.note: Stock-based.

name: Aloo tikki
description: Spiced mashed potato patties shallow-fried till crusted, served with chutneys.

tcm.note: Fried potato with warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from frying; potato is shita.

description: Grilled eel glazed with sweet soy over rice — a summer stamina dish.

tcm.note: Eel is warm and strongly tonifying in TCM; eaten in midsummer for stamina.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Pre-grilled eel and a decades-old tare in some shops — the reduction is deliberately never finished.

name: Ramen
description: Alkaline noodles in a broth simmered for hours, with toppings that vary by region.

tcm.note: Long-simmered bone broth with noodles.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Hours of bone broth plus soy or miso tare, plus cured pork on top — high on every layer.

name: Tsukemen
description: Cold thick noodles dipped into a concentrated hot broth, kept separate.

tcm.note: Cold noodles, very concentrated hot broth.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: The broth is reduced harder than ramen's, which concentrates everything in it.

name: Yakisoba
description: Wheat noodles griddled with cabbage and pork in a sweet fruity brown sauce.

tcm.note: Griddled noodles in a thick sauce.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the frying and sauce.

histamine.note: Yakisoba sauce is a fruit-and-vinegar reduction close to Worcestershire.

name: Okonomiyaki
description: A cabbage-heavy batter pancake griddled thick and covered in sauce, mayo and bonito.

tcm.note: Griddled batter with egg and cabbage.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna; the cabbage is shita beneath.

histamine.note: Egg, bonito flakes, mayonnaise and a Worcestershire-style sauce — four contributors on one pancake.

nutrition.highlight: cooked how you like it, as the name says

name: Takoyaki
description: Batter spheres with a piece of octopus inside, turned in a dimpled pan.

tcm.note: Fried batter with seafood.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; anda and seafood together.

histamine.note: Octopus, egg batter, bonito and sauce.

name: Tempura
description: Ice-cold batter fried so briefly the coating stays pale and shatters.

tcm.note: Deep-fried; the batter is barely cooked.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Prawn and egg batter; the dipping sauce is dashi-based.

nutrition.highlight: pale, not golden — that is the skill

name: Tonkatsu
description: Pork loin in panko, deep-fried and sliced, with a thick fruity brown sauce.

tcm.note: Deep-fried breaded pork.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru.

histamine.note: Egg in the coating, and tonkatsu sauce is a fruit-and-vinegar reduction.

nutrition.highlight: sliced, so you can pick it up

name: Karaage
description: Chicken marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted in starch and fried twice.

tcm.note: Marinated and fried poultry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Soy and sake marinade, usually overnight.

name: Yakitori
description: Chicken threaded on bamboo and grilled over charcoal, salted or glazed.

tcm.note: Charcoal-grilled poultry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; grilling is the most heating method.

histamine.note: The tare glaze is a long-kept soy reduction; the salt version is much lower.

name: Teriyaki
description: Meat or fish glazed with soy, mirin and sugar reduced until it shines.

tcm.note: Soy-glazed and pan-seared.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Soy and mirin reduction — the shine is the point and the problem.

name: Sukiyaki
description: Thin beef and vegetables simmered at the table in sweet soy, dipped in raw egg.

tcm.note: Sweet soy simmer with beef.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Soy, mirin and a raw egg dip.

nutrition.highlight: dipped in raw egg, at the table

name: Shabu-shabu
description: Paper-thin meat swished through plain kombu broth for seconds, then dipped.

tcm.note: Meat cooked seconds in a plain kelp broth — the lightest hotpot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the mamsa; the broth adds nothing.

histamine.note: The broth is only kombu, so this is far lower than a soy or miso hotpot — the dipping sauces decide it.

name: Oden
description: Fish cakes, egg, daikon and konnyaku simmered for hours in light dashi.

tcm.note: A long light simmer; daikon and konnyaku are cooling, the fish cakes warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the fish and egg.

histamine.note: Processed fish cakes held hot for hours in dashi — the convenience-store pot has been simmering all day.

name: Miso soup
description: Dashi with miso whisked in off the heat, plus tofu and wakame.

tcm.note: Fermented soybean in a warm broth.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and salty, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: Miso, dashi and wakame — three of the highest ingredients in the set, in the most ordinary bowl in Japan.

nutrition.highlight: the most ordinary bowl in Japan

name: Chawanmushi
description: Egg and dashi steamed into a barely-set savoury custard, eaten with a spoon.

tcm.note: Steamed egg in a light broth.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna.

histamine.note: Egg liberator plus dashi.

name: Gyoza
description: Thin-skinned dumplings fried on one side and steamed on the other.

tcm.note: Fried and steamed pork dumplings.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Soy in the filling and the dip both.

name: Onigiri
description: A triangle of salted rice around a filling, wrapped in nori.

tcm.note: Salted rice with a small filling.

ayurveda.note: Shita, following rice.

histamine.note: Depends on the filling. Plain salt or umeboshi are the extremes — one is nearly nothing, the other is a fermented pickle.

name: Japanese curry rice
description: Thick sweet roux-based curry over rice — closer to a stew than anything South Asian.

tcm.note: A roux-thickened spiced stew.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the spice and fat.

histamine.note: The roux blocks are heavily processed and the curry is famously better the next day.

nutrition.highlight: closer to stew than to curry

name: Omurice
description: Ketchup fried rice wrapped in a thin omelette, with more ketchup on top.

tcm.note: Fried rice and egg.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna.

histamine.note: Egg plus a great deal of ketchup, which is concentrated tomato.

name: Korokke
description: Mashed potato and mince in panko, deep-fried into a flat oval.

tcm.note: Fried breaded potato.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Egg in the coating, and the brown sauce on top.

name: Nikujaga
description: Beef and potato simmered in dashi, soy and mirin until the potato collapses.

tcm.note: Slow soy simmer.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Dashi and soy, simmered long and usually eaten the next day.

name: Kinpira
description: Burdock and carrot cut into matchsticks and braised in soy, sesame and chilli.

tcm.note: Burdock is cooling, the chilli and sesame warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the chilli and sesame oil.

histamine.note: Soy-braised.

name: Hijiki nimono
description: Rehydrated hijiki simmered with carrot, abura-age and soy.

tcm.note: Seaweed-led; cooling.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with the sea vegetables.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with seaweed.

histamine.note: Dried seaweed plus soy.

name: Ohitashi
description: Greens blanched, squeezed and steeped in cold dashi with bonito on top.

tcm.note: Blanched greens, served cold.

ayurveda.note: Shita.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; read with the leafy greens.

histamine.note: Spinach is usually the green, and it steeps in dashi — both rate high.

name: Sunomono
description: Cucumber and wakame dressed in sweetened rice vinegar, served very cold.

tcm.note: Raw cucumber and seaweed in vinegar, chilled.

ayurveda.note: Shita; a summer side.

histamine.note: Wakame and vinegar together.

name: Tamagoyaki
description: Layers of sweetened egg rolled in a rectangular pan into a striped block.

tcm.note: Egg, cooked gently.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna.

histamine.note: Egg liberator plus dashi in the batter.

name: Agedashi tofu
description: Tofu dusted in starch, fried, and sat in warm dashi broth.

tcm.note: Tofu is cool; frying warms it.

ayurveda.note: Shita, following soy.

histamine.note: Dashi and soy broth over the tofu.

nutrition.highlight: crisp, until the broth gets it

name: Hiyayakko
description: A block of chilled silken tofu with ginger, spring onion and soy poured over.

tcm.note: Tofu is cool and moistening; served cold, in summer.

ayurveda.note: Shita — one of the coolest dishes in the set.

histamine.note: The tofu is nearly nothing; the soy and bonito on top are what rate it.

name: Ochazuke
description: Hot green tea or dashi poured over leftover rice with a salty topping.

tcm.note: Green tea over rice — light and cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; read with rice and green tea.

histamine.note: Depends on the topping; the plain tea-and-rice base is very low.

name: Zosui
description: Rice simmered in the leftover hotpot broth until it thickens — the end of the meal.

tcm.note: Rice cooked in broth.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the broth.

histamine.note: Made from broth that has been simmering all evening.

name: Natto gohan
description: Fermented soybeans stirred with soy and mustard over hot rice.

tcm.note: Fermented soy over rice.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: Natto and soy together — one of the highest-histamine breakfasts there is.

name: Saba shioyaki
description: Mackerel salted, rested and grilled until the skin blisters.

tcm.note: Oily fish, salted and grilled.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Mackerel is a scombroid — the classic histamine-poisoning fish, and salting it before grilling adds time.

name: Buta no kakuni
description: Pork belly simmered for hours in soy, sake and sugar until a chopstick goes through.

tcm.note: Long soy braise.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru.

histamine.note: Hours of soy and sake braising — and the sake is a DAO blocker.

name: Daifuku
description: Soft pounded mochi wrapped around sweet red bean paste.

tcm.note: Glutinous rice, which is warm and binding.

ayurveda.note: Guru and hard to digest.

histamine.note: Very low — rice and bean paste, nothing fermented or aged.

name: Dorayaki
description: Two small honey pancakes sandwiching red bean paste.

tcm.note: Baked batter with honey.

ayurveda.note: Anda and madhu are both ushna.

histamine.note: Egg in the batter.

name: Taiyaki
description: Fish-shaped waffle batter filled with red bean, custard or chocolate.

tcm.note: Griddled batter.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the egg and sugar.

histamine.note: Egg batter; the custard filling adds more.

name: Dango
description: Rice-flour balls on a skewer, grilled and glazed with sweet soy.

tcm.note: Grilled glutinous rice with a soy glaze.

ayurveda.note: Guru; the glaze is ushna.

histamine.note: The mitarashi glaze is soy-based.

name: Anmitsu
description: Cubes of agar jelly with red bean, fruit and black sugar syrup.

tcm.note: Agar and fruit, served cold.

ayurveda.note: Shita; a summer dessert.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Castella
description: A dense honey sponge cake with no butter — Portuguese by origin, Nagasaki by adoption.

tcm.note: Baked egg and honey sponge.

ayurveda.note: Anda and madhu are ushna.

histamine.note: Egg-heavy.

name: Melonpan
description: A sweet bun under a crackled cookie crust — no melon involved.

tcm.note: Yeasted bread with a baked sugar crust.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Yeasted dough and egg.

nutrition.highlight: no melon in it at all

name: Purin
description: Steamed egg custard under a bitter caramel — firmer than crème caramel.

tcm.note: Steamed egg and milk.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna over a shita milk base.

histamine.note: Egg liberator.

name: Warabimochi
description: Translucent jelly squares of bracken starch, dusted in kinako and syrup.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; a plain starch jelly, read as cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita and light.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the starch jellies.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Senbei
description: Rice crackers grilled or fried and brushed with soy.

tcm.note: Grilled rice with a soy glaze.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the soy and grilling.

histamine.note: Soy-glazed, and often wrapped in nori.
